01 / Your objective

A sale within 60 days, with renting as the alternative.

Your priority is to complete a sale within 60 days of listing. If that cannot be achieved, your preference is to return the property to the rental market. The recommendation therefore emphasizes a competitive launch price, early feedback and enough time for a buyer to complete inspections and financing.

Recommended strategy · Target closing within 60 days

Recommended asking price

$329,900

Anticipated sale-price range: $320,000–$330,000

This range reflects your home’s larger floor plan, two-car garage and completed building improvements, balanced against its interior position, rear setting and current competing listings. Sale prices are before buyer credits, selling expenses and any loan payoff.

Timing objective: secure a qualified buyer within approximately 14–21 days and target closing within 45–60 days of launch. These are planning targets, not guaranteed outcomes.

Because the 60-day window is firm, this recommendation favors the more competitive launch price. The goal is to attract a buyer early enough to close, rather than spend most of that window testing the market.

What “sold” means: this plan targets a completed closing within 60 days, not simply a signed contract. Financing, appraisal, inspection and title issues can affect that timing, so price and closing reliability should be evaluated together.
02 / Your property’s position

Meaningful advantages, with realistic expectations.

Strengths to emphasize

Two-car garage. Seven of the nine comparable townhome sales and all three active competitors in this selection have one-car garages. Your additional bay is a practical advantage for parking and storage.

Additional living space. At 1,722 heated square feet, your home is larger than all nine selected townhome sales, which range from 1,508 to 1,662 square feet.

Completed exterior improvements. The HOA has just completed a new roof, new windows and new stucco on the building containing your unit. These improvements strengthen presentation and may help address concerns about near-term exterior maintenance.

Vacant and updated. Flexible showing access, a reasonably updated interior and the ability to offer possession without coordinating a tenant’s move can make the purchase process simpler.

Considerations reflected in pricing

Interior-unit position. End units can offer additional natural light, separation and outdoor exposure. Their sale prices should be considered with that advantage in mind.

Rear pond setting. The rear pond provides a natural backdrop, but its current appearance may not have the same appeal as a maintained water view or landscaped open space. We have treated the outlook as a pricing consideration rather than a premium feature.

Buyer alternatives. Vacant one-car townhomes are offered at $305,000 and $325,000. Your additional space, garage capacity and building improvements help distinguish the home, while a competitive price encourages buyers to act.

Presentation matters. A clean, welcoming patio and well-kept landscaping within your control can improve the first impression of the rear area. Any work on association property should be coordinated with the HOA.

The completed building work is based on information provided by Pamela. Obtain the HOA’s scope, completion documents, warranty details and assessment status for buyer review. No assumption is made that an assessment has been paid in full. The rear-setting observation concerns visual appeal; no wildlife hazard, drainage problem or environmental defect has been verified.

How we considered the differences

We gave the most weight to same-community sales and recent nearby transactions. Additional living area and the second garage bay favor your home; an end-unit position favors a comparable. The new roof, windows and stucco strengthen your condition story, while the rear setting moderates the price.

The selected sales do not isolate a reliable dollar amount for each feature. We therefore use a pricing range and qualitative reconciliation rather than claim that a garage, window project or pond outlook has a precise, proven value.

Why early pricing matters

Vacancy makes showing access easier, but several vacant properties in this selection still had lengthy market exposure. The records do not support a guaranteed vacancy premium or a blanket penalty for occupied homes.

10709 Savannah Landing is instructive: it contracted in eight days in its final campaign, yet had 297 cumulative market days. A competitive price can produce action; a low days-on-market figure after relisting does not erase earlier exposure.

05 / A defined selling window

Make the decision points clear from day one.

WhenPlan
Before launchConfirm heated square footage and garage details; assemble HOA improvement records, warranties and assessment information; confirm fees and HVAC condition. Complete photography and prepare the home for easy showings.
Day 1Launch at $329,900. Highlight the two-car garage, 1,722-square-foot layout, completed building improvements and vacant availability.
Days 7–14Review qualified showings, repeat visits, offers and consistent buyer feedback. If activity is weak, make an early pricing decision within the recommended sale range while there is still time to close.
Days 14–21Target a signed contract with a qualified buyer and a closing date within the 60-day window. Compare credits, contingencies and financing strength along with price.
By day 30If no viable contract is in place, review whether a timely sale remains realistic and prepare the rental fallback. Do not spend the remaining month waiting without a clear decision.
Days 45–60Complete the sale if the transaction is on track. If the home remains unsold and is available to lease, end the sale campaign and transition to rental marketing, coordinating around any existing sale contract.
Rental fallback: If the property has not sold within the agreed window, your preference is to rent it rather than extend the sales campaign. Rental pricing should be reviewed against current rental competition when that decision is made. This report does not establish an asking rent. Sale and rental marketing should be handled as separate, coordinated phases.
06 / Basis of this analysis

Prepared from your property details and the supplied MLS records.

Property information supplied by Pamela: 1,722 heated square feet, three bedrooms, two-and-a-half bathrooms, a two-car garage, interior-unit position, vacant availability, a reasonably updated interior and recently completed HOA roof, window and stucco work on the building. The rear setting was described as having weaker visual appeal.

The analysis uses Quick CMA9438.pdf (two pages) and 360_Property_View3180.pdf (43 pages), with listing status as of October 7, 2026. All 14 selected entries were reviewed; two detached homes were excluded. The subject is not one of the detailed listings. MLS area and timing fields can differ across listing histories; current sale-record areas are used consistently here.

The supplied selection contains no pending sales and no larger townhome sale to bracket your home’s size. No independent inspection, subject photo set or HOA completion documentation was provided. Refresh competing listings and verify material facts before launch. Condition, view and feature differences are reflected in the recommendation without assigning unsupported exact premiums.
